claim: Exact BMVZ seed-pair occurrence in a hardness-preserving augmented family
statement: Starting from a constant-color bounded-degree 5-local QMA-hard layered family H_base=sum_chi v_chi H_chi, add the two BJSW five-qubit seed projectors P_phi and P_psi on fresh ancillas as separate singleton colors of weight 1/4 each, scaling the original color weights by 1/2. Then H_aug=(1/2)H_base tensor I+(1/4)P_phi+(1/4)P_psi and lambda_min(H_aug)=lambda_min(H_base)/2. BMVZ Definition 1.6 allows positive layer weights and its small-layer rule repeats singleton clauses, so the exact repeated clauses Q_(v,T)=I-(I-|v><v|)^{tensor T} occur at every iteration. This does not establish membership in the particular unmodified canonical BJSW term table.
inputs_and_costs: The original family, its bounded-degree coloring, and the BMVZ weighted layered/path interface are supplied. The augmentation adds only 5 fresh qubits and two 5-local projectors; each new seed qubit has incidence two. Color count stays constant and minimum color weight stays bounded below. The QMA promise thresholds scale by exactly 1/2.
proof_status_and_falsifier: The common kernel of the two rank-one seed projectors has dimension at least 30, so the minimum energy of their sum is zero and the tensor-sum minimum separates. A failure of the source's positive layer-weight/small-layer rule or of the stated color interface would falsify the BMVZ membership step.
limits: The abstract BMVZ definition does not certify the pair in an unmodified input or adjacency list. This is a constructed augmented family. It is not an encoding theorem or novelty claim.

claim: Pair-only repeated seed has a constant-comparison sparse logical lift and a reversible-cube gap tradeoff
statement: For T repeated BJSW seed blocks, V|psi>=2^(-T/2)sum_x|x>U_x|psi>, with U_x=tensor_i U_(x_i), and B=I_branch tensor [I-tensor_i(I-|0^5><0^5|_i)] give a positive diagonal 1-row-sparse operator whose compression E=I-tensor_i(I-Q_i), Q_i=(P_phi+P_psi)/2, obeys q_-H_pair<=E<=q_-^(-1)H_pair, where H_pair=(Q_(phi,T)+Q_(psi,T))/2 and q_-=(1-1/(2sqrt(2)))/2>0.32. Every reversible uniform-cube kernel with jumps of at most q coordinates has Poincare gap at most 2q/T. Its Clifford-covariant connector has gap at most q/T and row support at most 1+s*8^q for degree s. Thus polynomial row support forces gap O(log(T)/T) within this connector class.
inputs_and_costs: The T-bit branch register and T five-qubit data blocks have polynomial size. V is a product controlled-Clifford circuit; B has diagonal 0/1 entries and an O(T)-time row/entry procedure. For a degree-s connector with maximum jump q, the row bound is 1+s*8^q. The bit-flip walk has row support at most 1+8T and connector gap 1/T.
proof_status_and_falsifier: The compression follows by averaging independent branch bits. The local nonzero eigenvalues of Q_i are q_- and 1-q_-; product principal cosines bound the pair Hamiltonian on the complement of its common kernel. For the gap bound, signed coordinate sums have variance T and sign-averaged Dirichlet form at most 2q. A counterexample reversible kernel violating this Rayleigh bound, or a failure of the stated Clifford row count, would falsify the tradeoff.
limits: Only reversible covariant branch-graph connectors on the pair interpolation are covered. Arbitrary positive enforcers, non-Markovian C, active data-workspace isometries, and the complete augmented hard list are not ruled out.

claim: Direct branch frames with branch-dependent pure workspaces require a wide exact enforcer row
statement: For V|psi>=sum_c sqrt(w_c)|c>U_c|psi>|a_c>, with w_c>0 and normalized pure workspace vectors a_c, let mu be the maximum absolute matrix entry between distinct monomial-equivalence classes of branch frames. If there are at least two classes, every matrix C with ker C=ran V has a computational-basis row with at least ceil(1+1/mu) nonzeros. For the two repeated BJSW frames, mu=2^(-3T/2), giving ceil(1+2^(3T/2)) even with arbitrary branch-dependent pure workspaces.
inputs_and_costs: Finite-dimensional logical and workspace registers are arbitrary in size. The branch amplitudes and pure workspace states are arbitrary. The theorem needs exact kernel equality but not C positivity or a quantitative gap; the target positive-gap condition implies its kernel premise.
proof_status_and_falsifier: Collapse each enforcer row by branch workspace amplitudes. Rank comparison forces a nonzero dependence among at least two representative frame rows; Gershgorin's criterion makes every set of fewer than ceil(1+1/mu) such rows independent. An explicit direct-frame counterexample with a narrower exact enforcer would falsify the lemma.
limits: This exact bound is for the two seed branches. It is not an exponential-row lower bound for the whole BMVZ list: the maximum coherence across all path branches may remain constant, and one branch per color does not encode the within-color path average. Data-dependent workspaces and active isometries are outside the theorem.

claim: Whole-list path-history encoding achieves exact constant logical comparison but only an inverse-polynomial image gap
statement: For an explicit polynomial-size BMVZ clause list flattened to R fixed-k local algebraic projectors, with exact local diagonalizers U_i and diagonal projectors D_i, a polynomial clock-history isometry V and positive contractions B,C exist with ker C=ran V, V*BV=(Q/K)H where 1/4<Q/K<=1, row support at most 1 for B and 9 for C, and C>=[(1-cos(pi/K))/2](I-VV*). The relative decoder factors across R disjoint blocks; each factor acts on at most 2k qubits and has a constant-size exact one-/two-qubit algebraic decomposition. K is polynomial in the clause count, transition-gate count and common weight denominator, so the gap is Theta(K^-2), not constant.
inputs_and_costs: The exact local term-matrix representation is part of the input interface and is polynomial-bit algebraic. The output has n'+log_2 K qubits. V has a polynomial-size controlled local-gate circuit. B has a polynomial-time diagonal entry oracle; C has at most 9 entries per row and a polynomial-time row/entry oracle. C terms act on the full log_2 K clock plus at most 2 data qubits; B's D_j can be global on the data. Hence constant locality is not established. Exact local diagonalization and two-qubit gate synthesis are polynomial in bit height for fixed k; C coefficients have polynomial bit height and constant algebraic degree under the stated input model.
proof_status_and_falsifier: The clock positions repeat each clause decoder for q_j=Qw_j tail positions and insert relative local gates between tails. Each C edge is positive. Gauge conjugation gives one quarter of the path Laplacian, yielding the stated exact kernel and gap; averaging B over tails gives (Q/K)H. A matrix entry, kernel, or compression counterexample to these identities would falsify the construction.
limits: This is a complete positive sparse-row lift under the explicit exact local algebraic-matrix representation; approximate-entry-only inputs need an additional perturbation proof. It reaches only inverse-polynomial gap and growing clock locality. It does not meet constant gap, constant locality, or quantum-PCP requirements.

claim: Independent L02 zero-spectrum and mixed-exposure audit
statement: The resolvent Jensen comparison at zero spectrum is operator-norm safe by epsilon shifts and ||F_(T+epsilon)-F_T||<=sqrt(epsilon), while POVM transport uses bounded regularizations with strong convergence and von Neumann algebra closure. The mixed exposure law is normalized only after including transported vector norms; the component barycenter requires the Pinsker drift term. The checked threshold constants remain 2048 for disconnected support and 1024 for connected support.
inputs_and_costs: Bounded positive effects on arbitrary Hilbert spaces and finite positive ensembles are allowed. No bounded inverse on a support projection is used. This audits proof steps, not source acquisition or an external referee process.
proof_status_and_falsifier: The audit reconstructs the resolvent identity, positive Gram domination, zero-spectrum limit, algebra-preserving transport, exposure mass identity and component KL drift. A counterexample to one of those displayed inequalities or an algebra-membership failure would falsify the audited proof route.
limits: No formalization, external validation, priority claim, named verifier consequence, or Hamiltonian/PCP implication is established here.

claim: The N26 positive local syndrome obstruction is a scoped interface, not a general common-encoding no-go
statement: For K_x=sum_a w_a E_(a,x|S_a) on a fixed common auxiliary space, w_a>=0, sum_a w_a=1, 0<=E_a<=I and |S_a|<=r, if inf spec K_0<=eta and K_x>=cI for every nonzero x in {0,1}^t, then c<=eta+(r/t)(1-eta). In particular, exact completeness requires r>=ct for constant normalized gap. The proof does not apply to sector-coupling, x-dependent auxiliary embeddings, signed/global-positive decompositions, or a general sparse positive matrix without this positive local budget.
inputs_and_costs: The same auxiliary space, fixed weights, positive contraction effects, and all nonzero Boolean syndrome sectors are required. Arbitrarily large or infinite auxiliary dimension and noncommuting effects are allowed. The bound is independent of dimension and is sharp.
proof_status_and_falsifier: Choose an approximate ground vector for K_0. A term is unchanged on singleton e_i when i is outside its set S_a; averaging the singleton energies charges at most r coordinates per unit positive budget. A legal example violating the inequality under these exact premises would falsify the theorem.
limits: The result is an internal prior card, with external priority unestablished. The common positive sparse encoding target may use sector coupling, active workspaces, or global positive matrices, so this result does not settle that gate.

claim: Any positive sparse enforcer of the fixed full-list history image has a repetition-dependent gap upper bound
statement: Let P be the exact kernel projection of a finite positive contraction C<=I with first positive eigenvalue gamma and maximum row support s. If a row i has projection mass at least m on J and each squared entry on J is at most a, then for D=log(m/(2a))/log(s+1)>1, gamma <= [log(8/m)/(4(D-1))]^2. For the augmented BMVZ singleton seed tails in the banked full-list uniform-history image, chosen Clifford decoders give (m,a)=(q/K^2,1/(K^2*8^T)) with q=Q/4. More generally, for any factorwise decoders across the T seed copies, the fixed overlap |<phi,psi>|^2=1/8 gives a selected row with every squared relative entry <=(7/8)^T, hence (m,a)=(q/K^2,(7/8)^T/K^2). This yields gamma <= [log(8K^2/q)log(s+1)/(4(log(q*(8/7)^T/2)-log(s+1)))]^2 whenever D>1. The result also covers decoders that mix the full base data copy, provided endpoints factor across copies and diagonalize P_phi tensor I and P_psi tensor I. For T dominating log K+log s the bound is O((log K log(s+1)/T)^2); it tends to zero when T>>log K log(s+1), in particular for K,s<=n^b and T>=n^c with fixed positive exponents.
inputs_and_costs: Finite-dimensional positive contraction, exact kernel projector, row support s, and the stated projector-row mass/entry bound. The application uses the explicitly augmented two singleton seed layers, history length K, repeated seed count T, and exact BMVZ seed overlap. No decomposition of C, row oracle, reversibility, covariance, or locality assumption is needed. The arbitrary-decoder extension needs factorwise endpoint decoders across T copies; they may act on the entire base data copy. It excludes constant all-state gap for polynomial row support on these fixed uniform-history images, including basis-injective monomial classical workspace recodings.
proof_status_and_falsifier: Degree-l Chebyshev filtering approximates P in operator norm by 2 exp(-2l sqrt(gamma)); a degree-l polynomial in C has row support at most (s+1)^l. Any omitted target projection-row mass bounds approximation error below. Choosing l=ceil(log(8/m)/(4sqrt(gamma))) yields the formula. For arbitrary factorwise decoders, the selected phi row has one entry of square 1/8 by the seed overlap and unit row norm, so every entry square is at most 7/8; tensoring yields (7/8)^T. For a full-base-copy decoder the identity P_phi P_psi P_phi=(1/8)P_phi gives the same row cap. An exact sparse positive contraction for the same image with a gap violating the bound, or a failure of the seed-tail projector-row data, would falsify the claim.
limits: The no-go applies only to the exact uniform-history image with factorwise endpoint decoders across T copies, and survives basis-injective monomial recodings. It does not cover a global decoder of the amplified OR projector, coherent quantum workspace maps, or redesigned isometries; it does not constrain logical B and does not imply a quantum PCP result. The separate Clifford stabilizer construction has a constant-gap enforcer, so this cannot be generalized to all Clifford images. External proof validation and novelty remain UNKNOWN.
